review:
I can't help but be dissapointed by this game. Other reviews seem to hype it up like it's some kind of amazing stealth experience, but in reality it's a 4 hour long Call of Duty stealth segment. Linear to the point of absurdity (they literally point you to your targets and say "shoot this guy, now shoot this other guy, great, now these two guys" for the entire game), it has no depth whatsoever, and the story is as interesting as bingo night with your grandma.

Seriously one of the most underwhelming games I've ever played.

Okay so this is my very first proper review on a game,and although this game is so old that i doubt anyone will actualy read this,I still want to give my thoughts on what I found to be a fairly enjoyable game.I`ll go over the good and the bad,mostly regarding the single player.I feel like the MP is far too basic to be considered a driving force as to what makes this game good or bad.(although the MP was by no means boring,just stale and has little going on)
It would be fair to start with the good,but in this case I disagree,I feel like theres enough bugs to scare away quite some people,so I`ll start with that.

Sniper Ghost Warrior 2 is by no means new,but for its time period I definetely expected more attention given to some fairly annoying bugs,none of them are completely game-breaking,most are just minor details the devs probably missed,but there are some God awful bugs that should have been patched the day they were found,and that simply never happend.

In my 20hrs of gameplay of chievo collecting,I discovered a couple,but some players get lucky and never come across a single bug,its a risk worth taking though.The bugs I encountered were the following:

 -Character would crouch and immediately after he would stand up without any command to do so,at several points of setting up 50 cal. rifle,the character would simply not pull any gun out,and I`d have to restart the mission (sometimes I`d be stuck in binoculars too),character would refuse to go prone at specific spots (it was flat area,and should have allowed me to prone).Sometimes the character refused to let me aim with either sniper or sidearm,simply had it in his hand but I couldnt use it.When following a npc (objective being to follow that npc),sometimes the npc would simply stand in the same spot and never continue walking.
 -These are honestly as annoying as they are minor,I wasnt too bothered by having to reload a checkpoint or restart a mission.But the worst part of this was the no sound glitch..Fucking hell this was so annoying,I played through literally HALF of the game with NO gameplay sound,only cinematics had sound,sometimes background music would play while in game and disappear again at the next checkpoint,this bug alone is enough to make me reconsider weather or not the gameplay was good,it should have been immediately fixed the moment it was found out,but simply wasnt give due attention by devs.I also navigated forums to see if I could find a fix for it,and tbh I didnt try any of the suggested fixes (the authors usually said it never fixed the issue anyway).I gave up,blasted some metal music or talked to my imaginary  gf while I played and accepted my fate,around the last mission of act II it came back and stayed for good,never encountered the same issue since.I find this specific problem to be a massive downside to the game,so be warned that its a possibility you'll encounter this same issue,or maybe you're one of the lucky ones.

With the bugs out of the way,lets talk gameplay and story.I was actually quite impressed with the gameplay,the gun recoil feels somewhat realistic,the variety is enough to make each act feel different,the guns have a satisfying feel with each kill,and even the sidearm was fun to play with.I also quite liked the stealth knife kills,that was a lot of fun.The game heavily encourages stealth,and it forces you to place your shots carefully,not every enemy is an obstacle unless they are directly in your path,and this makes the missions feel like you have room to different playstyles as far as sniping goes.Can either go stealth and sneak by,or eliminate each and every soul that dares breathe,up to you.The shots are also not straight forward,the wind and distance heavily affect the outcome of each shot,and if playing on expert,you might have to carefully calculate your shots,lest avoid missing and causing havoc.The maps also give you room to be creative with your kills,taking different spots gives different advantages,this detail is sometimes key to clearing an outpost swiftly and quietly.Speaking on maps,woah,I really liked the maps the game offers,from the swamps of act I to the ruins of a war-wrecked city in act II.The maps are beautifully made and have enough variety to make them exciting,as well as decently big,sort of.

I should also add,please play this on expert?This difficulty is barely hard and the others literally show a red dot indicating bullet drop,it makes the game stupidly easy and I found it so annoying that I was being hand-fed my shots.

The story was..bearable?I dont know if I'd say the story was a leading factor as to why I enjoyed the game,if anything it was quite comedic,the way you and the other characters interact verbally is so unprofessional that I had quite a laugh from it,hearing your captain say "Job well done,but you're still an asshole" made it feel like the script crew wasnt exactly aiming for anything but a joke,but I cant complain,at least it wasnt stale and boring,instead it either put a smile on my face or made me cringe.The story was boring,no plot twists actually an effect on me,I didnt feel any attachment towards any characters,nothing.The story fails to build a bond with whats happening in the story-line.The biggest bond I had was with my rifle.So take that for what it is,if youre looking for an exciting story,this isnt the game for you.The gameplay itself is the real climax to this game,not to mention it also looks quite decent for the time it was released.

I feel like thats saying enough regarding the single player.I have to say,buy this at your own risk,the bugs can be intolerable,but if you can look past that,then you have a fairly enjoyable game to get through,not to mention the chievos are easy to get anyway!I would like to give higher,but the bugs and lack of excitement in the story dont allow for much.The real saving factor of this game was the fun gameplay and decent design.So I will set my personal critic at 6.5/10.

[b]Sniper: Ghost Warrior 2 is not your typical run-and-gun FPS. It’s a game that tests your patience, discipline, and love for precision shooting. Where most shooters reward speed and aggression, this game demands silence, timing, and planning. Having spent dozens of hours with it, I can confidently say, if you’re into stealth and tactical gameplay, this is a true hidden gem.[/b]

[h1]Gameplay & Mechanics:[/h1]
[b]Unlike mainstream shooters, patience is your greatest weapon here. Lining up the perfect shot requires careful observation of wind, distance, and enemy movement. Every pull of the trigger feels earned.[/b]
[list]
[*][u]Stealth Above All:[/u] Rushing in will get you killed. Shadow movement, cover, and timing are the real keys to survival.

[*][u]Ballistics Simulation:[/u] Bullet drop and wind effects make long-range shots highly satisfying when executed correctly.

[*][u]Cinematic Kill-Cams:[/u] Landing a long-distance headshot never gets old, and the cinematic camera adds extra flair to your precision.
[/list]
[b]“Real Masterpiece for Stealth Players. Tip: Don’t Buy if you don’t like waiting.”[/b]

[h1]Story & Atmosphere:[/h1]
[b]The campaign takes you across jungles, snowy mountains, and war-torn cities. While the narrative isn’t groundbreaking, it creates enough immersion to keep you moving forward. The real star here is the tension-filled atmosphere, sneaking past enemy patrols, waiting for the right moment, and pulling off the perfect synchronized takedown.[/b]

[h1]Graphics & Sound Design:[/h1]
[b]For its release period, Sniper: Ghost Warrior 2 looked visually impressive. Environments are lush and detailed, and the use of CryEngine really shines in lighting and terrain design. The sound design also elevates the experience, from the distant echo of your rifle to the whisper of suppressed shots, the audio pulls you into the sniper’s world.[/b]

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Deeply rewarding stealth & sniping mechanics

[*]Realistic bullet physics (wind, distance, bullet drop)

[*]Tense, immersive atmosphere with cinematic kill cams

[*]Beautifully rendered environments (CryEngine still holds up decently)

[*]Satisfying for players who enjoy patience-driven gameplay
[/list]
[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Pacing may feel too slow for run-and-gun FPS fans

[*]AI can be inconsistent (sometimes sharp, sometimes clueless)

[*]Story is serviceable but not very memorable

[*]Linear mission design reduces replayability

[*]Definitely not for players who dislike waiting or stealth-heavy gameplay
[/list]
[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
[b]Sniper: Ghost Warrior 2 is not for everyone, and it doesn’t try to be. It’s not Call of Duty, it’s not Battlefield, and it doesn’t want to be. Instead, it’s a dedicated sniper’s experience, built around patience, timing, and precision.
If you love stealth shooters and the satisfaction of a perfect long-range kill, this game is a masterpiece of its niche. If not… well, you’ve been warned.[/b]

I reviewed Ghost Warrior 2 four years ago and gave it a negative evaluation. I have decided just recently to revisit the title as I remember the campaign was left unfinished. Surprisingly, I had a lot of fun so much so that I decided to purchase its story-oriented expansion pack titled Siberian Strike. Let's look at the game in more detail!

[u]Graphics:[/u]

This is definitely a step-up compared to its predecessor which used Chrome Engine 4. The guys at City Interactive decided to license CryEngine 3. The game looks much, much better and, frankly, I still find it beautiful even today. The lush forests of the Philippines or the huge Tibetan areas we traverse in the last act all look very detailed and just good to look at. The 3 acts have an entirely different artwork due to the different locations - attention to detail is very good in this game.

[u]Story:[/u]

Still somewhat mediocre but the new scenery in an upcoming act certainly keeps the gamer engaged. Overall we have 3 acts to capture a bad guy called Merinov. Things become interesting when the 2nd act takes us back to the past (Sarajevo, 1993) to tell more information on the background of our hero, Cole Anderson. What makes the game great is the constant radio contact between Anderson and HQ and his pal, Diaz. This back and forth with the inclusion of some witty one-liners help forget that the game lacks any decision-making on the player's part as it is very, very (and I mean very) linear.

[u]Gameplay:[/u]

I already mentioned Ghost Warrior's linear gameplay but one thing is for sure: you can forget about the machine gun sections that made its predecessor extremely annoying and difficult. As the title suggests here we are truly snipers and when not sniping a pistol with a suppressor and melee takedowns with a knife will come in handy. This approach serves the game better - several levels can be completed by being a "ghost".

[u]Multiplayer + Misc.[/u]

Non-existent. There were some people playing it 4 years ago and I was able to join some sessions but overall multiplayer is completely dead. As for the 'cheevos: There are some nice campaign-related achievements so you can replay some of the chapters if you are an achievement hunter. Also, some of the collectibles are very well hidden!

[u]Summary[/u]

Ghost Warrior has always been a somewhat mediocre title - like a B movie. Still, if you are finished the Sniper Elite series and would like to try something new until the next big hit in this genre is out Ghost Warrior is a good choice. Its story is very linear but the sniper and spotter duo makes it work like a movie. This is a more refined version and a sequel I can only recommend. Often discounted and available at a very low price. Mark Wahlberg (from Shooter) gave it a thumbs-up!

I would give this game something between a thumbs up and a thumbs down because I do like some aspects of the game.  However, they force me to make a black & white choice and I choose "No Way".  The graphics are pretty good, the basic gameplay is OK but there are a lot of issues:

1.  There are places on the maps you can get stuck and not be able to get out of AND you cannot kill yourself to continue playing the game!  You have to leave the game altogether and rejoin (if you can).

2.  There is no way to kick or ban a player on your own server DURING the game ...you have to wait for the game to be over!  This is the ONLY thing you can do to protect yourself and it isn't even in-the-moment or real-time!

3.  Rampant cheating via engineered hacking/aimbot/God-mode programs ruin any opportunity for the expectation of fair play.  I feel as though I have left more games than I have finished because of these jerks.  I wish them all a horrible painful death in the real world.  They have collectively stolen the money we have invested in this game and Steam does nothing to stop it.  Indeed, the cheaters occasionally talk about such things and defend their own actions on the Discussion channels and you never see a Steam moderator step in and take any action.  They have left us to the wolves.

4.  The "game-view" or "sight-view" (what you see vs. what the enemy sees) is really screwed up.  I can be inside a tunnel with no view of the enemy yet he can see me and kill me.  How is that fair?  My arms and legs aren't hanging out, I am OUT OF SIGHT and even this is no defense.  Being out-of-sight is not even considered stealthy in a game that is BUILT on concept of stealth?

5.  There is no way to configure your own server for "Pistols-Only", "No Pistols" or anything else that would allow different styles of play or game modes for variety.  Every server and every map is largely identical with few deviations.  It quickly  becomes boring.

6.  Character movement and control is full of inconsistencies... in some places you cannot go prone for no aparent reason.  Where you can go prone, while you are crawling on your belly you may encounter a flat board or step in the ground.  Crawling across this change in terrain causes you to STAND UP!  Instant death in many circumstances.  Other places with boards or terrain changes this doesn't happen and you pass right through them.  In some places you cannot go prone, but if you hit "Crouch" it instantly goes prone instead.  VERY inconsistent on a portion of the game that SHOULD be rock-solid in its second version.

7.  Cheaters/hackers/banned players can just make up a new name and continue playing.  How does this help the integrity of the game?  There is no way to stop them and the game LETS them get away with it for as long as they want.

An “ok” non-AAA game that provides a mainstream stealth and sniping experience.

Presentation and writing are mediocre and clichéd, but I was already expecting this. Otherwise, the story is not bad, and slightly more down-to-earth than most Call of Duty games of late. Levels are very linear and heavily scripted. You are guided by your spotter who stays at your side most of the time. This provides good immersion and manages to convey the sense of working as a team, but his AI is a bit unreliable when in open combat.

The scripting is fairly basic and lacks some polish. There were various issues, like dialogue getting cut off, or checkpoints not reloading correctly. A few times my character would confirm over radio that I had the target in my crosshair, but the target was no where to be seen on my screen. The checkpoint save system has the usual irritations associated with such a system. It is also a pity the difficulty settings offer no more options beyond “easy, medium, hard” - I wanted to play “medium”, but without the “red dot” aim assist that ruins the sniping challenge. Also, once you have started, there is no option to change the difficulty later. I had a few crashes to desktop. All these issues were very annoying, but did not ruin the experience.

The graphics are decent (as you would expect from the CryEngine) but do not quite have the same visual quality as the Crysis games. Some areas look really nice, but others less so. The standard quality setting are poorly optimised. I achieved much better fps after careful tweaking (tip: put “object detail” on low for massive fps boost and next to no quality loss).

Controls are ok, but feel a bit clunky and are unresponsive in some contexts. Fortunately there is no mouse lag or acceleration. Weapon handling and ballistics are ok, but not simulator grade. The game lacks a detailed tutorial and you cannot “zero” the sights to various ranges like you can in ARMA and Red Orchestra 2. The simulation of wind on bullets feels artificial because the wind speed is not effectively reflected in the environment - vegetation does not respond accordingly and there are no other indicators like the sound of wind or moving dust etc. The displayed distances seem to be fake - an ingame distance of 400m is actually closer to 200m (a sin many mainstream games commit one way or another to be more accessible to console peasants). Compared to Far Cry 3, this game was clearly made on a smaller budget, with less content, freedom and polish, but in the end I still liked the single player campaign more here. It is more cohesive and serious, while Far Cry 3 was a theme park of absurd sensationalist violence.

Overall this is a decent second-rate game I mildly enjoyed. I had very modest expectations, and it satisfied them. Get it when on sale.

Developed by polish City Interactive and motored by Cryengine 3, Sniper: Ghost Warrior 2 wants to be your typical tactical shooter, but doesn't quite make it.

Sniper: Ghost Warrior 2 takes place in Philippines, when a group of mercenaries, including you, have been hired to destroy an old radar post.
On your way you hear an enemy radio chatter about a spy working to the same team as you.
Mission quickly turns into a duty to safely capture your own man, who is being held captive.

Gameplay-wise Sniper: Ghost Warrior 2 doesn't really shine. Practically every mission feels like same, without any kind of variation. You drop into place A, and then proceed to place B, all whilst taking out enemy soldiers.
Game offers you an option to pick a preferred gameplay style. You can swap between styles any time, and it doesn't affect the game story-wise. You can go in guns blazing or hide in the shadows and camouflage to your surroundings. They even added some stealth kill mechanics, so you can also act like your modern day assassin.

Wouldn't call plot of the story bad, just about mediocre. The game also is very short. I took 5 hours to complete story mode.
Sniper: Ghost warrior 2 is currently priced in steam at 9,99€. I'm not sure if you should even pay more for this game. The quality-price ratio seems fine. Simply said you get what you pay for.

One word: CryEngine.
The game engine ruins the whole experience. It’s very poorly optimised; the environments are carefully crafted but look awful up close, and the animations are very poorly done...

The game itself is rather mediocre. The storyline is uninspired and quickly forgotten. Act 2 is completely pointless.
The cutscenes could easily have been integrated into the gameplay, as most of the time you’re just watching your character play. 
The gameplay is meant to be almost open-ended and free, BUT the game is scripted – right down to choosing your targets – so it’s not much fun to play.

The AI couldn’t be any more daft. The enemies are completely deaf, at times as blind as a bat and at others with vision that would put the Terminator to shame.

I won’t even mention the continuity errors and absurdities of that sort (such as a section where you’re supposed to be silent but your teammate is screaming just 2 cm away from the enemies, ...).

It’s a shame because the developers have really improved their game since the first one, and you can tell a lot of work has gone into it – the environments are well-crafted, and the characters are too. The developers need to keep going down this path and they’ll achieve something!

If one looks for a game that has to do with actual sniping, look no further: This is absolutely not it, and the only game which is that is the ArmA series (with the right mods and missions and/or people to play with).

This game has about as much to do with being a sniper as Carmageddon has to do with being an everyday commuter by car. Unfortunately not only the gameplay - which pretty much forces you to shoot your way through most of it - has nothing to do with sniping, but neither does anything else the devs have put into this game.

It supposedly is about a "ghost" warrior. I presume that they mean a creator of ghosts, because there'll be a shitload of them around after he's done murdering half of the country he's in. The things that one would think that "ghost" actually refers to are about as silly as the All Ghillied Up mission in COD4, although that game actually did it kind'a good.

The "ghostyness" of this game includes:
 - Your spotter/buddy approaching a gate saying "We've got to be careful.", and when you as the player open the door he'll run through it (and the next 100 meters of who knows what) like it was the start signal for olympic 110m hurdles. Running around seems to be an important theme in sneaking, according to this game.
 - Leaving a trail of bodies so rich and dense that a blind-deaf old man could track you down by the smell of blood and gunpowder alone.
 - Careful sneaking to stay hidden (with the scripted AI), in places where the sun will show your shadows like huge silhouette figures against the wall beside you, rather than sneaking 2-3 meters away where there is room to sneak. Also shouting and arguing within earshot of the enemy is also fantastic stealth-behaviour.
 - Having a 'sniper perch' inside of a building where the character leans through the window, instead of sitting well inside of the room to hide himself, seems to be preferable. No sport in being a sniper if the enemy can't see you, right?
 - Firing with an unsuppressed Barrett rifle from just a few hundred meters so that everyone within at least a mile's radius ought to be able to locate you by the sound alone, not to mention all the dust-kickup from that muzzle brake.
 - Having such a ghosty sight so that on the highest difficulty where you get no aim assist there is no scientific way to determine where to aim. The mils-scale on the sight is completely useless, so you just have to wing it and hope you hit. 

Despite all the above the game is almost okay though, as long as one expects an on-rails shooter. Although the game is heavily scripted and basically breaks if you don't do shit in the order you are supposed to, it plays quite fine if you stick to the script. It is testosterone-pumped to the point of stupidity; the characters are so full of it that they almost explode, but main grips of the story are still good enough to feel plausible and game-progressing. The game can be pretty tricky on the hardest difficulty too because almost all your UI-help from the easier modes is gone, so finding that particular object or guy to shoot that your buddies are asking you to pop can be very hard sometimes.

The game is flawed. Pretty darn flawed actually. But for the €2 I paid for it on this summer sale I don't feel like I was tricked. I definitely got my money's worth of fun, but it would be senseless to buy this game for its full €10.

I really can't whole-hartedly recommend this game. It is an enjoyable enough sniper game, especially if you're looking for a cheap alternative to Sniper Elite or the like, but damn does it have its flaws. Get ready to hear every one I can remember.

First off, you might as well ignore the story. Spoiler alert: [spoiler]every character they focus on besides the player is a back-stabbing traitor. There are literally 3 traitors in this one game.[/spoiler] The guy giving orders before/during the missions is your typical "Dammit man, get it done at all costs! I don't care about your emotions!" obnoxious military general. Just to drag it out, on multiple ocassions you have your finger on the trigger about to do the deed and captain-impatient tells you there's no time and you have to do something more important.

The cutscenes are full of bad voice-acting, worse motion-capture, and half are entirely useless. [spoiler]At one point you're knocked out and taken hostage during a cutscene. You wait for a second cutscene to load and play [i] immediately [/i] afterwards, wherein you wake up and get punched in the face and knocked out again. Riveting stuff.[/spoiler] All in glorious 480p resolution. [spoiler]Oh, and when you wake up from capture and free yourself, you immediately find a handgun which your character specifically comments has 4 rounds in the magazine, you kill an enemy right outside the door, he drops his assault rifle right on the ground and you can't pick it up. Just brilliant.[/spoiler]

The gameplay and AI is just horrendous. During one mission, your first target is a sniper who's standing (yeah, standing) in a bell tower, totally motionless. I take the shot, bullet passes right through his head, no damage, suddenly everyone in the whole town knows my GPS coordinates. Eff this, reload last checkpoint. Try again, this time the bullet goes THROUGH HIS FACE, blood splatter and everything, he falls out of the goddamn bell tower AND LIVES. My character comments something to the effect of "Dang, I missed and now he knows I'm here." 'KAY. Reload checkpoint, try again, exact same outcome. No idea what's wrong with this game.

And for a sniper game that involves a lot of crouching and prone, they sure as hell made it impossible to do that. Let's say Z is crouch and X is prone, right? If you're crouching and hit the prone key, nothing happens and nothing indicates that your posture has changed. But when you hit the crouch button again, you go prone. Press crouch again, you stand up. Crouch again, you crouch. Press prone twice while crouched, you stand up. You wind up just pressing Z and X in random patterns to eventually wind up in the position you were looking for. It makes no sense at all.

As for the missions, for more than half you are hand-held by an ally as you follow them needlessly-close to enemies and have no choice or challenge in taking a different route or finding your own way. It's just bad. Let me sum up how the game plays: During one mission, you go through a parking garage packed with hostiles. You are tasked with shutting down the lights and sneaking out using your night vision while the enemies are blind. You have one route to take to the fuse box, thereby forcing you to perform a scripted knife kill along the way. Stab enemy (the stealth kill animations are also atrocious btw), look to the right, [b][i]remember the lights are still on at this point[/i][/b], there's another hostile not 25 feet away looking right at you with no visual obstructions, and he doesn't notice. Alright then. Proceed to the fuse box, RIP THE WIRES OUT BECAUSE THAT'S HOW FUSE BOXES WORK, and head for the exit. All the way to the exit, you can pass 5 feet in front of enemies and they can't see you because it's pitch black. At one point I thought "There's no way I can get past this guy, I'll be 2 feet from his face, I'll just kill him instead". Wait for the area to be clear of other enemies, stealthy knife kill from behind in the inky black darkness, suddenly EVERY ENEMY KNOWS I'M THERE AND CAN MAGICALLY SEE ME, I get lit up and die next to a rusty old car.

That's this game.

4/10

Except for few moments, there is no challenge either as long as you keep it low profile.

That kind of linearity can be advantageous since it can help developers focus on story and presentation. Think about CoD campaigns (the good ones). SNIPER: GHOST WARRIOR 2 IS A CLASSIC TITLE WHERE PERFECT AIM IS A REWARDING SENSE OF ACHIEVAL
-REVIEWED ON: (GeForce GT 1030/i7-3770 )

- I really enjoyed this one, and plan to play the rest of the games in the franchise whenever I can. This game is simple, and yet challenging for all audiences who aim for tougher difficulties.  This said, let's break it all into points of interest:

PLOT AND FEEL: The game's story is basic from start to finish, brothers in arms on a mission with some thrilling cutscenes and an obvious twist in the genre. The game operates  as Ghost Recon or Rainbox Six at times where communication is a need, so it's important to listen to your comrades so as to not f*ck it up and make it to the end. The game puts you in the shoes of the protagonist Captain Cole Anderson, which is sent on a mission to the Philippines with his bro Agent Diaz. You'll be playing as him throughout the game, getting to know him, his codes by the book, and his team. There is not much background to his or the other soldiers involved, but it's enough to get to know him as the man he is. 

LENGHT: The game is short, and includes three acts lined up in specific chapter segments. I advise everyone to enjoy the game fully before reaching the end, because the finale is clean but generic. Thus you will probably feel a sense of emptiness. 

PERFORMANCE: The game ran well for me, and after so many years optimization was not an issue regarding graphics and smoothness. 

BUGGY BUT PLAYABLE TO THE END: From the start and up until the conclusion casually, I came across some annoying checkpoint bugs that requires restarting that said moment in order to complete the mission. This mainly happened when I rushed into mission objectives leaving Diaz behind and trying to focus on the task at hand by my own will. Diaz would just be there kneeling and doing nothing, when he has to actually lead you into objectives at all times and you have to obey and follow. By restarting the checkpoints and carefully executing every command I was able to beat the missions. Maybe you guys should keep this in mind just in case it happens to you as well.

A TEST OF PRECISION AND MECHANICS: Just like the title of the game, "sniping" takes knowledge, aim, precision, experience, and patience. The game even in casual mode will test your hands on the rifle as a priority, and every bullet counts for a prevented mistake. In fact, to get 100% accuracy you must use one bullet for all enemies on each mission. I believe I only achieved this in one chapter.  Even if at short or long distances, your breathing skills will be a need at times and you will fail to deliver clean shots if not careful with your grasp and aim. This will cost you and your partner since you or both will alert enemies. Do take note, that failing to deliver a clean shot may result in death depending your current position and health. Enemy pathing is sometimes unpredictable, so they will try to flank you or corner you, you can as well use this strategy to advantage. Luckily you have a silencer handgun and rifle most of the time, so you can change your gameplay and adapt casually.  Just like in games like Dishonored, full stealth is not a requirement. But you're not Corvo with supernatural skills, so going all out on your enemy will be a horrible approach. This is not a game where you can 1V9 and get away with it quickly, I died many times just to rage and see where it got me. But it does give you the freedom to retaliate whenever you made a mistake and gun down the rest of enemies. Most of the game you are free to finish a mission in aggressive or passive ways, so feel free to experiment.  All in all the game's mechanics, surroundings, and enemy response makes the experience quite realistic and defying. 

-While I was here for the story and to try something new, I enjoyed my time even with some bugs and not aiming for much more than I got. But for those of you interested in achievement hunting and re-playability, there is more to do in higher difficulties and there seems to be a multiplayer mode with rewards as well.  Quite a fun FPS game, even with a weak character development or story 9.8/10

Sniper: Ghost Warrior 2 is a significant improvement over the first game. The graphics are better, the sound design is stronger, the presentation feels more modern, and overall it immediately gives a better first impression. Compared to the original release, there is a clear evolution in production quality.

Unfortunately, once the novelty wears off, many of the same problems begin to appear again.

The biggest issue is that the game still struggles with the very thing it is built around: sniping. The shooting mechanics often feel inconsistent, especially during longer-range engagements. Bullet drop and ballistic systems exist, but they rarely feel reliable. There were numerous situations where shots appeared to hit enemies directly, only for nothing to happen. Sometimes enemies survived shots that should have been lethal, while other times bullets seemed to pass through targets entirely.

The AI creates another layer of frustration. Friendly NPCs can walk through enemy positions without being detected, while enemies occasionally spot the player through vegetation, objects, or angles that shouldn't realistically provide visibility. These situations make stealth feel artificial rather than tactical and often break immersion.

The game presents itself as a sniper experience, but rarely captures the feeling of being an actual sniper. The missions are extremely linear, and while linear design isn't necessarily a problem, the game lacks the tension, planning, and satisfaction that usually define the genre. Instead of rewarding precision and patience, many encounters feel scripted and simplistic.

What makes this disappointing is that the improvements are easy to see. The developers clearly invested effort into the visuals, atmosphere, and overall presentation. However, the core mechanics received far less attention. The result is a game that looks much better than its predecessor but still struggles to deliver a convincing sniper experience.

In the end, Sniper: Ghost Warrior 2 is better than the first game in almost every technical aspect. The problem is that the foundation remains largely the same. For players looking for a genuine sniper-focused experience, there are simply better alternatives available.

I really think that this is an excellent sniper game because they went with authentic realism with this one. Yes, the game is pretty linear, but that doesn't mean that it's bad or that it isn't enjoyable for what it is.

By authentic realism, I mean that it seems everything in the game is modeled in a very realistic way, from game levels and things that are and are not interactive. For instance, the vehicles in the game look real, like how they would be in the real world. Enemies and enemy equipment are also plausible, and then things that you have control over, like the sniper rifles and especially their scopes, are really well done. I do not like that in later iterations of the franchise, they deviated from this formula. For instance, the scopes in SGW: Contracts 1 and 2 really look bad and take up a lot of the screen when you use them. Whereas in this game, they look really good and have a good scale to them. Basically, many things in the game are rendered well in that regard of scaling because things in the game seem to be based on real things, making the game feel like you're handling real objects, as opposed to dealing with artistic impressions that you may or may not align with.

The graphics of the game are okay, and the gameplay is pretty good. I like the linearity of this game more than the semi-open world nature of its successor, SGW 3, because it's kind of tedious to have to drive around the map to get from place to place, and enemies just keep respawning each time you cross a line in the map at sights like various gas stations, enemy outposts, and ultimately mission destinations. So the linearity of this game is a welcome change to that formula, which they have admittedly improved on with the SGW: Contracts games. Sound is also pretty decent. I like how the 9mm sidearm sounds; when you shoot it, you first hear the bullet going through the silencer and then the [i]click-clack[/i] from the slide action. Likewise, the silenced sniper rifles sound really good, but they are both too quiet in close quarters, like the enemies do not react to your weapons when you use them. But that's fine, really—just a little nitpick.

I like how the game portrays the life or duties of a US army sniper. Again, the authenticity seems to be really plausible, and I appreciate that a lot because all these realistic and plausible elements make the game very immersive. I have to emphasize once more that it's kind of a pity that they deviated from this formula in later games. Although a change is welcome, we don't really get a lot of games like this one—sniper games that are authentic to a level seen in this game. That is also one of the reasons why I wanted to write a review about it and recommend this game, even though the game does show its age in regards to the graphics and overall narrow level design. Nonetheless, it's a very enjoyable experience with pretty good and smooth gameplay. For instance, the bullets feel like they actually have some weight to them, meaning they are very effective and deadly, whether from the sidearm or the sniper rifles. If you like that from a game experience that is both immersive and fun to engage with, then do not overlook this game, because you'll have to experience it if you like these things I have tried to describe here.

Levels and missions are, I think, well designed; they are okay and functional, and pretty cool to go through in no small part due to the story, which can be perceived as bad. Whatever— to me, again, it comes down to authenticity. The game reminds me of why we enjoyed linear games in the past. There is just something special about the nature of such games that, compared to open-world games, is lacking because often open-world games just play out in the open and aren't really scripted in any particular way except to be a sort of sandbox. In open-world games, a lot of the buildings are often inaccessible, whereas places found in linear games just feel different. You can really notice this when playing games like Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light versus something like Metro Exodus or Ghost Recon: Breakpoint (though GR: Wildlands was pretty good for an open-world game). Again, in this sense, some progress is welcome in game design. Gaming has progressed from linear games into more open-world games, which is a nice thing, but open-world games aren't always as detailed as linear games used to be, which were sort of custom-tailored to really leave an impression on a person and make experiencing them a memorable experience because of the stories and environments.

I think Sniper Ghost Warrior is just that: a memorable experience that leaves me harking back to how games used to be (linear and scripted) in their design and makes me miss authenticity in some more modern sniper games. Relating to scripted game events, CoD games are full of them in single-player and are super popular with each iteration. This leads me to think that the nature of open-world games can't really touch on this aspect of interactivity and storytelling. In open-world games, AI behaves more dynamically and in a hive mind due to some apparent, noticeable limitations of AI in games. For instance, if you alert one enemy AI, all the enemies start converging on your location and start shooting. I appreciate that feeling from linear games where it feels more logical, like you are actually part of a story or ongoing events. Both types of games, open-world vs. linear games, have their distinct characteristics and appeal in their own ways, and Sniper Ghost Warrior 2 is one of those games I like precisely because it's linear but not necessarily limiting.

I picked this up during a sale for basically nothing, knowing it had a mixed reputation. After playing through the campaign, I can see exactly why opinions are all over the place. This is a game that does some things genuinely well, but the flaws are impossible to ignore.

Let me start with what surprised me: the sniping mechanics are actually solid. You have to account for wind, distance, and bullet drop, which adds a layer of realism that makes landing a long shot genuinely satisfying. When you nail a perfect kill, the bullet-cam follows the shot in slow motion—it never gets old . The game runs on CryEngine 3, and when it looks good, it really looks good. The jungle environments, the snowy Tibetan mountains, the war-torn streets of Sarajevo—these settings have real atmosphere .

But then the problems start piling up.

**The Good:**
- **The core sniping feels right.** The bullet physics are well-implemented. On higher difficulties, you lose the helper markers and actually have to judge wind and drop yourself, which turns each shot into a real calculation. That's when the game shines .
- **The atmosphere hits.** The Sarajevo mission in particular does a decent job showing the horrors of war. It's not subtle, but it's effective .
- **The Siberian Strike DLC.** I grabbed this separately, and honestly, it's a prequel mission that's arguably better than parts of the main campaign. If you end up getting the game, make sure to get the complete edition .
- **Shooting works on both keyboard/mouse and controller.** Controls are responsive and you can play whichever way you prefer .

**The Bad:**
- **It's incredibly linear.** This is the biggest issue. You're essentially playing on rails. Walk here. Shoot this man. Set up your rifle here. Sneak past these guards. The game rarely lets you make your own decisions . At one point you lose your rifle and have to retrieve it—but you can't pick up enemy weapons. You have to do exactly what the designers wanted, common sense be damned .
- **The campaign is short.** Around 4-5 hours for the main story. That's it .
- **The stealth is frustrating.** The AI is either blind or psychic. You can be perfectly hidden and suddenly everyone knows exactly where you are. When you get spotted, enemies rush you with reckless abandon and you'll probably die . Then you get sent back to a checkpoint that was 10 minutes ago. No quicksave option makes this painful .
- **The AI is also dumb.** If you miss a shot on easier difficulties, enemies react so slowly you have time to just shoot again. And somehow, no one hears the massive unsilenced rifle crack coming from 200 meters away .
- **Cutscenes look awful.** They're pre-rendered at low resolution with terrible compression, so you get visible pixelation that completely pulls you out of the experience . This is especially jarring because the actual gameplay visuals can be quite nice.
- **CryEngine 3 has technical issues.** The game can lock your framerate to your monitor's lowest refresh rate—some players got locked at 24fps. I ran into some stuttering and one or two crashes during my playthrough .
- **No weapon variety.** You can't pick up enemy weapons after they die. You're stuck with what you're given .
- **Multiplayer is dead.** Don't buy this expecting to play online. It's a ghost town .

**Quick Tips:**
- **Play on the hardest difficulty.** This is non-negotiable. On lower difficulties, the game holds your hand with red dot markers and giant icons over every enemy's head. It becomes a boring shooting gallery. On hard, those helpers disappear and you actually have to calculate your shots .
- **Grab the Siberian Strike DLC.** It's a full extra mission that adds some value. If you're buying the game, get the complete edition .
- **Manual save is not an option.** The game uses checkpoints only. They can be spaced poorly. Be prepared to replay sections .
- **Patience is required.** This is not a run-and-gun game. If you treat it like Call of Duty, you'll die constantly. Move slowly, scout before you shoot, and think about the order you take out enemies .
- **Buy it on deep sale only.** At full price, this is hard to recommend. For $5 or less? It's a weekend distraction if you're a sniper game enthusiast .
- **The original Sniper: Ghost Warrior had some freedom in its levels. This one is more restrictive—go in knowing that .

**Verdict:**

Sniper: Ghost Warrior 2 is a game caught between ambitions. It wants to be a realistic sniper simulation, but it also wants to be a cinematic Call of Duty-style shooter. The result is something that does neither perfectly.

If you're a sniper game fanatic who loves bullet physics and lining up long shots, there's fun to be had here, especially if you stick to the hardest difficulty. The core shooting mechanics are genuinely satisfying when they work.

But the restrictive level design, frustrating stealth AI, short campaign, and technical issues hold it back from being anything more than mediocre. The game actively fights your attempts to play creatively. Want to pick up an enemy's weapon when you're unarmed? Sorry. Want to sneak past enemies without killing them? The script won't allow it . Want to explore that jungle over there? "LEAVING MISSION AREA" .

Compared to Sniper Elite, which came out around the same time, Ghost Warrior 2 feels shallow. Sniper Elite has more freedom, better stealth mechanics, and those glorious X-ray kill cams. This game's bullet-cam is tame by comparison .

If you can find this for a few dollars and you're a fan of sniper games who doesn't mind a linear experience, you might enjoy it. Everyone else should look elsewhere.

Personally so far I think this is the best game CI Games have produced. As a sniper-enthusiast I look for pros and cons with this game. I have already in advance completed this game on the Xbox 360 a long time ago, and to be honest I felt more connected into the game, and more sort a say “Alive” on the PC version. Here are some reasons why.

1. With a decent good computer specifications, you can get amazing sniper experience. The graphics are stunning. As you would expect from the CryEngine. But It’s not quite the same visual quality as the Crysis games. Some areas look really nice, but others less so. Here is a screenshot captured by me in-game: http://imgur.com/IEv5urm Cut-scenes graphics are a bit poor, huge improvement can be done there, example: http://imgur.com/EpkAOPS

I achieved much better fps after careful tweaking (Tip: Put “Object Detail” on low for massive fps boost and next to no quality loss).

2. Having a headphone on you with Surround Sound makes you feel more realistic. I have tested it with speakers (Surround Sound), and I didn’t get nearly the same experience.

3. I would recommend you to play it with a Xbox 360 controller on the PC version - (If it’s possible). Sniper Ghost Warrior it’s actually a more of a console type of game when it comes to controllers. Kinda like GTA V, The Witcher 3, and the Call of Duty franchise. And I’m not saying it because I played the game first with a Xbox 360, but the whole movement with a mouse and keyboard makes it feel weird compared to a smoother version with a controller. Controls are ok, but feel a bit clunky and are unresponsive in some contexts.

4. Something I wasn’t aware of when I first played this game on the 360 console. I bought all of the DLC’s on the PC version, and I recognized the DLC called: Sniper Ghost Warrior 2: Digital Extras.The Special Edition Includes SOUNDTRACK - An official Soundtrack from the game’s musical score. It’s a nice soundtrack and has a nice beat to it in a close danger situation or a sticky situation. Your heart starts to beat a bit more and you get a little bit of the adrenaline kick. I think that’s a huge deal when it comes to sniper games.

Sidenote: I think that Michał Cielecki did a amazing job with the soundtracks. I really feel excited when I hear his soundtracks. I’m looking forward to see if he have any soundtracks to the Sniper Ghost Warrior 3. https://soundcloud.com/michal-cielecki

Generally about the game:

It’s a good non-AAA game that provides a stealth and sniping experience. Presentation and writing are a bit clichéd, but I was already expecting this. Otherwise, the story is not bad at all. Levels are very linear and heavily scripted. You are guided by your commander who stays at your side most of the time. This provides good immersion and manages to convey the sense of working as a team.

Cons/Improvements:

I’m not going to cover every specific detail about this game, but I’m going to cover some of it.

The scripting is fairly basic and lacks some polish. There were various issues. My AI was a bit unreliable when we went stealth mode - Here is actually a great example that I captured: http://imgur.com/D3hmFA6 On the picture you can see we were inside the tunnels in Bosnia Sarajevo. My teammate (Maddox) alerted me to hide because there were troops coming towards us. For some weird reason Maddox didn’t do anything (obviously he glitched out). After of certain of time Maddox starts yelling “Fuck! Run!!” when the guards are right in front of him. I had to restart my mission, because we were basically fucked when they had 10 guards pointing at us and firing. Lucky for me the checkpoint was right outside the tunnel. So I wasn’t needed to process the whole scenery (Before we went inside the tunnel again).

Sometimes when you got the order/mission from either your teammate or your commander to go backstabbing a guard. You could just literally run behind him and make a lot of footsteps without him recognize anything. Seems like these guards are partly death at some areas. They only recognized you if they saw you and if you shoot. Hearing running footsteps and other small details like reloading a gun was not intended apparently.

Dialogue were cutting off sometimes when you reached checkpoints.
A few times my character would confirm over radio that I had the target in my sight, but the target was no where to be seen on my screen. The checkpoint save system has the usual irritations associated with such a system. Checkpoints was not reloading correctly.

If you run down some stairs you just start floating a little bit above it instead of actually running on top of it. Kinda annoying effect http://imgur.com/sEyedLj. I also don’t like on the scene "Burning Bridges" (Act 3 - Mission 2) when you have to run from the temple and your stamina ends so often/quickly. Just like this: http://imgur.com/enuIHwO. I can understand that in reality it’s heavy carrying a sniper rifle around, but it’s kinda silly how Anderson survived there. In my opinion City Interactive could twisted this situation with other solutions.



The simulation of wind on bullets feels artificial because the wind speed is not effectively reflected in the environment - vegetation does not respond accordingly and there are no other indicators like the sound of wind or moving dust etc. The displayed distances seem to be fake - an ingame distance of 400 meters is actually closer to 200 meters. http://imgur.com/IEv5urm


Backdraw: If you just realized Sniper Ghost Warrior recently, I think you are going to be a bit disappointed in this game. Reason being is this game was released on March 12, 2013 in North America, March 15, 2013 in Europe and March 19, 2013 in Australia. They used not a old game engine to develop this game. But the singleplayer content is a bit slim compared to other games that are released in 2016. The game will approximately last 5 hours ish of gameplay. If you don’t care about these details that happens every now and then, and you are more into the main storyline in this game, I would recommend it. Be sure to follow some recommendations above to make this game even more enjoyable and I had very modest expectations, and it satisfied them. Get it when on sale.

[h3]Title: Sniper: Ghost Warrior 2[/h3]

Summary: Sniper stealth game

Personal notes: Sniper: Ghost Warrior 2 is a FPS game with a heavy emphasis on sniping. You are called a ghost warrior, and within a special ops unit, you use your skills to sneak, stalk, survey & snipe. This second entry builds directly off the foundation of first one quite well! You take on similar missions but this time with a stronger emphasis on presentation and a more focused experience, with sniping mechanics feeling more refined and cinematic overall making those long distance shots feel all the more rewarding. Visually, this game also is a clear improvement over the last entry. The environments are much more varied and detailed in contrast to the many similiar levels in the first. In addition to this, CryEngine was used instead of Chrome engine which made the game look much more modern. I will say these graphic improvements came at a slight cost of the environments feeling slightly less vast, because of this it can feel more linear with less paths. The AI is also improved upon but still isn't amazing and sometimes inconsistent. It felt better but was still frustrating at points due to unpredicatable enemy behaviours. This also made stealth more of a viable option but still isn't super consistent. Some encounters felt tense and rewarding while others felt like trial and error. Achievement wise, it's pretty straight forward with most being related to missions, difficulty or hitting a certain amount of kills. There is online achievements that are still atainable but the population is very low so I would recommend finding a friend/check the community to help you out with them. Overall, Sniper Ghost Warrior 2 delivers some solid sniping and improves upon the first entry but is still slightly held back by it's inconsistency and limited player freedom. I would recommend this to most FPS fans, especially if you enjoy slower, more tactical experiences. I would also recommend that you start on this game instead of the first entry as this is where the series really starts to build it's own identity.

💾Graphics - This is a huge step up from the previous game. The textures look great here, especially for the environment. The weapons look really sharp and the animations are a huge improvement. The UI is also a welcome change, making the game look more modern and still holds up even for today. For a 2013 game, this game aged pretty well and I'm pleased to see such a huge improvement from their previous game.

🎮Gameplay - There are some good mechanics here that are improved, but some are worse. Let’s start with the good. The breathing mechanics have improved here. It’s more predictable and makes more sense here. The stealth has also improved slightly (although not up to par still). The companions are actually helpful and help you eliminate targets pretty quickly. The sniping mechanics are still here (heart rate, breath holding, wind direction, bullet drop), and it makes the sniping super addicting. Bullet time is still present and it’s even better than before. Now for the bad, the AI are insane here still. Playing on expert mode, the AI will almost insta kill you here which feels BS in some situations. There is almost no weapon variety here, which is a shame because the weapons look great and have great animations. There are some issues, but if you play on Normal or Easy, you will have a far better experience than I did.

📜Story - The story felt really dull and forgettable. The characters are not memorable or interesting in my opinion. The plot felt weak and rushed. The main antagonist is a joke and I couldn’t take him seriously at all. It all felt rushed here! Speaking of rushed, you only have 3 Acts here. So not many missions and they feel kinda bland in my opinion. The Spotter system (which gives you a companion to spot for you) made the game way too easy. You will have many hand holding missions that were not enjoyable. At least the locations are really good here, as you get to see some pretty unique areas that many games don’t really show.

🕛Playtime - The story was around 5 hours of playtime. If you are playing on an easier difficulty, expect it to be shorter. You have multiplayer here, but no one plays it. So you will only have a 5-8 hour experience (if you have the expansion pack as well).

🎧Sound - The sound design is a big step up from the first game. The guns sound better here. They are not great, but an improvement which is a plus. The voice acting is a mix bag here. Some lines are corny and not delivered well, and some voice actors really sound cringy here. The sound track is actually pretty good! It’s not annoying, and it gives some sections a great feel of intensity.

❗Bugs❗- I haven’t really encountered many bugs here. Just mainly some minor ones. The only one that was annoying was that Vsync in the menu does not work, so you will have to look for a guide on this (sadly I couldn’t find one on Steam).

🔅Performance - Performance was great for me! I played on max settings (with Directx 9 enabled) and had no issues. I had zero issues with stutters or frame rate. If you have similar specs or maybe even a bit older, you should have no issues here.

You play as Captain Cole Anderson, a professional sniper who spends most of his working day lying in uncomfortable places and staring through a scope at people who have absolutely no idea they're about to have the worst day of their lives. So yeah, kiddo, 7/10.
